Population represented by each BDHS round, for pooling

Source: R/data.R
bdhs_pool_population.Rd

The national female population aged 15-49 at the reference date of each DHS round and the number of women interviewed. DHS weights are normalised so that they sum to the sample size of each round; when rounds are pooled, bdhs_pool() multiplies the weights of each round by female_15_49 / n_women_sample so that each round counts in proportion to the population it represents rather than to its sample size.

Usage

bdhs_pool_population

Format

A tibble with 9 rows (one per DHS round) and 9 columns:

survey_id

DHS survey identifier.

survey_label

Year label, e.g. "2017-18".

ref_year

Reference date as a decimal year: the mean interview date where the microdata were available to the maintainer, otherwise the midpoint of fieldwork (1996-97).

female_15_49

Female population aged 15-49 (persons): UN World Population Prospects 2024 estimate, linearly interpolated between the 1 July estimates bracketing ref_year.

n_women_sample

Number of (ever-married) women interviewed, from the DHS API.

women_age_min, women_age_max

Age range of eligible women.

p_ever_married

Proportion of women 15-49 ever married: 1 minus the DHS percentage never married (indicator MA_MSTA_W_NMA) / 100.

source

Sources of female_15_49 and n_women_sample.

Source

United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, https://population.un.org/wpp/ (CC BY 3.0 IGO); The DHS Program Indicator Data API, retrieved 2026-10-26. Built by data-raw/06-build-pool-population.R.

Details

BDHS women's samples are ever-married women; p_ever_married gives the share of women 15-49 who were ever married, should you prefer to scale to the ever-married population.

See also

bdhs_pool(), bdhs_surveys.

Examples

bdhs_pool_population[, c("survey_id", "ref_year", "female_15_49", "n_women_sample")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   survey_id ref_year female_15_49 n_women_sample
#>   <chr>        <dbl>        <dbl>          <int>
#> 1 BD1994DHS    1994.     28096489           9640
#> 2 BD1997DHS    1997.     30782776           9127
#> 3 BD2000DHS    2000.     33689291          10544
#> 4 BD2004DHS    2004.     36965636          11440
#> 5 BD2007DHS    2007.     39019159          10996
#> 6 BD2011DHS    2012.     41427050          17842
#> 7 BD2014DHS    2015.     43360901          17863
#> 8 BD2017DHS    2018.     45459595          20127
#> 9 BD2022DHS    2023.     48342561          30078

# Pooling weight multipliers
with(bdhs_pool_population, setNames(female_15_49 / n_women_sample, survey_id))
#> BD1994DHS BD1997DHS BD2000DHS BD2004DHS BD2007DHS BD2011DHS BD2014DHS BD2017DHS 
#>  2914.574  3372.716  3195.115  3231.262  3548.487  2321.884  2427.414  2258.637 
#> BD2022DHS 
#>  1607.240
